paper.title: Threshold-Based Optimal Arm Selection in Monotonic Bandits: Regret Lower Bounds and Algorithms

unmapped: Arm means strictly increasing mu_1 < ... < mu_K, ordering known to the learner
Known threshold tau in (0,1) with mu_1 < tau <= mu_K
Optimal arm is the first arm with mean >= tau (not the best arm)
Regret defined as sum_k |mu_{k*} - mu_k| E[t_k(T)]
settings.definition_quote: Threshold-crossing identification: given by k^*_{(1)} = \min \{ k \in S : \mu_k \geq \tau \} ... R^{\pi}(T) = \sum_{k=1}^{K} |\mu_{k^*} - \mu_k| \mathbb{E}[t^{\pi}_k(T)]

settings.name_in_paper: l-th above (below) threshold identification (monotonic bandits) (lower bound)
unmapped: Arm means strictly increasing, ordering known to the learner
Known threshold tau in (0,1) with mu_1 < tau <= mu_K
Optimal arm is the l-th arm above (or below) tau, l known
Regret defined as sum_k |mu_{k*} - mu_k| E[t_k(T)]
settings.definition_quote: \l^\th above (below) threshold identification: given by k^*_{(2,a)} = k^*_{(1)} + \l-1 (k^*_{(2,b)} = k^*_{(1)}-\l)

unmapped: Arm means strictly increasing, ordering known to the learner
Known threshold tau in (0,1) with mu_1 < tau <= mu_K
Optimal arm is the arm with mean closest to tau
Regret defined as sum_k |mu_{k*} - mu_k| E[t_k(T)]
settings.definition_quote: Threshold proximity identification: Given by k^*_{\text{cl}} = \arg\min_{k \in S} |\mu_k - \tau|.

algorithms.name: RTOSMB (Ranked-Threshold Optimal Sampling in Monotonic Bandits)
POSMB (Proximity-Focused Optimal Sampling in Monotonic Bandits)

symbols.mu_kstar: mean of the optimal arm k* = first arm with mean >= tau
symbols.mu_kprime: mean of arm k' = k*-1 (last arm below tau)

conditions: strictly increasing means with mu_1 < tau <= mu_K

source.label: thm:1
source.quote: Let $\pi \in \Pi$ be a uniformly good algorithm for the threshold-crossing identification problem. Then, for any $\theta \in \Theta_{\tau}$, \liminf_{T \to \infty} \frac{R^{\pi}(T)}{\log T} \geq \frac{|\mu_{k^*} - \mu_{k^\prime}|}{I_{\min}(\theta_{k^\prime}, \tau)}, where $k^* = \arg\min \{ k \mid \mu_k \geq \tau \}$ is the optimal arm, and $k^\prime = k^* - 1$.

results.notes: Regret defined through expected pull counts and |mu_k* - mu_k|, so pseudo-regret-like with nonstandard gaps. Lemma 1 extends to the 'arm just below tau' variant via inversion.

symbols.mu_kstar: mean of optimal arm k* = k' + l - 1
symbols.mu_kprime: mean of arm k' = first arm with mean >= tau
symbols.mu_kprime_m1: mean of arm k'-1 (last arm below tau)

conditions: strictly increasing means with mu_1 < tau <= mu_K

source.label: thm:2
source.quote: Let $\pi \in \Pi$ is a uniformly good algorithm for $\l^\th$ arm above threshold identification. Then, for any $\theta \in \Theta_{\tau}$, \liminf_{T \to \infty} \frac{R^{\pi}(T)}{\log T} \geq \frac{|\mu_{k^*} - \mu_{k'}|}{I_{\min}(\theta_{k'}, \tau)}\mathds{1}\{k^* \neq K\} + \frac{|\mu_{k^*} - \mu_{k'-1}|}{I_{\min}(\theta_{k'-1}, \tau)}, where $k' = \arg\min \{ k\mid \mu_k \geq \tau \}$, and $k^* = k'+\l-1$ is the optimal arm.

results.notes: The paper writes I_min but the proof uses the plain Bernoulli KL I(theta_k', tau) (I_min as defined would be 0 for theta_k' >= tau); recorded as kl. Lemma 1 extends to the l-th arm below tau.

symbols.mu_kstar: mean of the arm closest to tau
symbols.mu_kadj: mean of arm k = k*-1 if mu_{k*} >= tau, else k*+1

conditions: strictly increasing means with mu_1 < tau <= mu_K

source.label: thm:3
source.quote: Let $\pi \in \Pi$ is a uniformly good algorithm for threshold proximity identification problem. Then, for any $\theta \in \Theta_{\tau}$, the regret bound is: \liminf_{T \to \infty} \frac{R^{\pi}(T)}{\log T} \geq \frac{|\mu_{k^*} - \mu_{k}|}{I_{\min}(\theta_{k}, 2\tau - \theta_{k^*})}, where $k^* = \arg\min \{ |\mu_k - \tau|\}$ is the optimal arm, and k = k^*-1 if \mu_{k^*}\geq \tau, k^*+1 otherwise.

results.notes: Proof uses plain Bernoulli KL I(theta_k, 2tau - theta_k*). No upper bounds are proved for TOSMB/RTOSMB/POSMB (only simulations).
